title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive

tasks.short: Answer calls, provide routine information, record messages and connect callers to the right person.

steps.what: Answer the call and establish the caller's needs.
Find contact details or approved information for the caller's request.
Explain the answer, check understanding and handle questions.
Record a message and send it to the requested recipient when needed.
Transfer the caller when a suitable recipient is available.

tasks.design: Configure a searchable directory and approved answer cards in the {DOCS}, using only permitted directory fields from the {HCM}. Configure message forms and transfer shortcuts around the {TELEPHONY}, with internal messages delivered through the {EMAIL}. The assistant handles the conversation and selects what information to disclose.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact lists and answer documents were scattered. Keeping them current required cooperation across departments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, forms and telephone controls cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can make small connectors cheaper to build; no new model capability is required.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising urgency, protecting private information and finding someone who will take an unusual call.
tasks.human_edge: Hear distress, understand an unclear request and make the caller feel heard.

ambition.what: A callback service for unanswered calls, with a named recipient and due time.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less searching and message copying. The assistant can prioritise callback follow-up within agreed service rules; authority to disclose information does not expand.

reach.task: Review repeated routing failures and adjust reception coverage.
reach.learn: Service measures, call categories and staffing constraints.

evidence.claim: Directory search, structured message forms and telephone shortcuts can reduce handling effort without a model.
GDPR requires appropriate access, purpose limitation and retention for caller and employee information.

assumptions: This is a human reception service, with no automatic caller conversation or recording.
The directory exposes approved business contact fields, not unrestricted employee records.
Messages and transfers are alternative branches; shares represent their average contribution across calls.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors, not measured savings.
unknowns: Whether the {TELEPHONY} supports message forms, directory lookup and transfer shortcuts.
Who maintains approved answers and contact availability.
Actual call mix, handling time and frequency of sensitive inquiries.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be answered from a short, approved reference?
Can existing configuration supply the directory without a custom connector?
new_work: Update contact destinations and approved answers.
Follow up overdue callbacks and failed transfers.
Check access permissions and message retention.
tasks.statement: Answer telephones and give information to callers, take messages, or transfer calls to appropriate individuals.

tasks.short: Welcome visitors, understand their needs, contact hosts and give appropriate directions or information.

steps.what: Welcome the visitor and establish their purpose and intended host.
Check the appointment, host details and relevant visitor instructions.
Tell the host that the visitor has arrived.
Confirm whether to receive the visitor or arrange another response.
Give directions, explain the response or help the visitor with remaining questions.

tasks.design: Configure an arrival form in the {WORKFLOW} that retrieves permitted visit details from the {CALENDAR} and instructions from the {DOCS}. It notifies the host through the {CHAT} and records their response before reception directs the visitor onwards. Reception keeps the welcome and handles unexpected needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reception depended on calendar access, separate instructions and informal messages to hosts.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, calendar permissions and notification flows are established capabilities. Small integrations can now be built and adjusted at lower development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected visitors, absent hosts, language barriers and situations requiring discretion.
tasks.human_edge: Make visitors comfortable and adapt assistance to their circumstances.

ambition.what: A pre-arrival assistance service for visitors who request accessibility support.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time locating hosts and chasing replies. They can coordinate requested visitor assistance within agreed limits; hosts retain decisions about receiving visitors.

reach.task: Arrange accessible routes and visitor assistance.
reach.learn: Building access, accessibility arrangements and escalation contacts.

evidence.claim: Calendar lookup, arrival notifications and explicit host responses can use deterministic workflow configuration.
Visitor records need proportionate collection, restricted access and defined retention under GDPR.

assumptions: This task primarily covers physical reception; telephone handling is described in the separate call task.
Reception checks appointments without seeing unrelated calendar content.
Shares cover active handling across participants and exclude visitor waiting time.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Assistance requests record practical arrangements rather than unnecessary health details.
unknowns: Whether visit appointments are available to reception in the {CALENDAR}.
Current host approval and building access arrangements.
Languages, visitor volumes and accessibility needs.
Applicable national rules and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can a calendar-derived visit list replace repeated appointment searches?
Which host responses and fallback contacts should the arrival form offer?
new_work: Maintain host fallback contacts and visitor instructions.
Handle unmatched appointments and unanswered notifications.
Review visitor record retention and coordinate requested assistance.
tasks.statement: Greet visitors or callers and handle their inquiries or direct them to the appropriate persons according to their needs.

tasks.short: Find the correct supporting files and attach them to correspondence prepared for reply.

steps.what: Read incoming correspondence and identify the request, subject, and relevant record references.

loop.input: Incoming correspondence and permitted reference formats.
loop.output: Requested information, record references, and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate reference formats and identities; display supporting correspondence passages.
loop.stop: One extraction; ambiguous identities or missing references return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reference parsing handles standard identifiers, but requests also describe needs in free text.

steps.what: Search authorised folders and records for candidate supporting files.
Check relevance, version, completeness, and whether files may be shared with the intended recipient.

loop.input: Permission-filtered candidate files, reply requirements, version metadata, and recipient details.
loop.output: Proposed attachment set with relevance passages and unresolved disclosure questions.
loop.check: Apply version and sharing rules deterministically; assistant verifies relevance and recipient entitlement.
loop.stop: Inspect at most ten candidate files once; unresolved relevance or disclosure questions require manual selection.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata checks establish versions and permissions, but cannot always establish relevance to a narrative request.

steps.what: Attach selected files to the reply draft and pass it to the reply owner.

tasks.design: A bounded intake step extracts request details from the {EMAIL}, then an integration searches the {DOCS} using references and permission-filtered metadata. A second bounded step proposes relevant files, while deterministic checks enforce version and sharing rules. The assistant approves the attachment set before the {EMAIL} receives a reply draft for its owner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent file names, missing record references, and fragmented permissions make reliable retrieval difficult. Relevance often depends on reading the request.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration development makes permission-aware search and draft assembly affordable. Small language steps can interpret requests and explain candidate relevance.
tasks.still_hard: Poorly indexed archives, scanned files, duplicate versions, and recipient entitlement remain difficult. Internal read access does not establish permission to disclose externally.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognises when an apparently relevant file exposes unrelated information or answers the wrong question.

ambition.what: Source-linked reply preparation for field coordinators.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching folders toward checking difficult evidence and disclosure questions. The assistant gains no new disclosure authority; a proposed service extends preparation support to field coordinators.

reach.task: Improve document references, version labels, and retrieval metadata.
reach.learn: Records classification, retention schedules, and access-control inheritance.

evidence.claim: Reference-based retrieval, permission filtering, version checks, and draft attachment assembly can use deterministic technology.
Narrative relevance suggestions need source references and human checking before disclosure.

assumptions: Most supporting files are electronic; paper-only archives remain a manual exception.
The document store exposes searchable metadata and enforceable access controls.
The workflow prepares attachments; the reply owner controls sending in the adjoining reply process.
The assistant may approve routine attachment selection under established sharing rules; unclear disclosures go to the information owner.
Build ranges cover one shared mailbox and one document repository.
GDPR applies to search, processing, and disclosure. National rules determine any consultation required for changed working methods.
unknowns: Document-index quality, scanned-file volume, and duplicate-version prevalence.
Whether search interfaces preserve the requesting user's permissions.
Available recipient-entitlement rules and information-owner escalation routes.
Whether attachment versions can be pinned between approval and draft creation.
research_questions: How much retrieval succeeds using record references and metadata alone?
Does relevance assistance reduce total search and checking time?
Can the attachment process detect changed files or recipients after approval?
new_work: Review ambiguous requests and proposed file relevance.
Repair metadata and resolve duplicate versions.
Maintain sharing rules and permission mappings.
Handle changed files, failed attachments, and disclosure escalations.
tasks.statement: Locate and attach appropriate files to incoming correspondence requiring replies.

tasks.short: Receive physical and electronic correspondence, route it, and answer routine letters.

steps.what: Open physical mail and separate named, confidential or damaged items.
Scan paper correspondence using scanning equipment and save digital copies.
Read scans and incoming messages to identify purpose, urgency and responsible team.

loop.input: Unmatched correspondence, an approved routing directory and sensitivity rules.
loop.output: Proposed team, urgency, sensitivity flag and reply requirement.
loop.check: Require a valid team and supporting text; deterministic rules override classification.
loop.stop: One classification per item; ambiguous, sensitive or conflicting results enter a human queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender and subject rules handle known traffic, but unfamiliar prose requires interpretation.

steps.what: Forward digital correspondence and deliver physical originals to the responsible recipient.
Draft routine replies using previous letters, templates and current information.

loop.input: Correspondence, approved information and the applicable reply template.
loop.output: Reply draft with missing facts and proposed commitments marked.
loop.check: Validate names, dates and references against records; reject unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft; missing facts or complaints requiring judgement go to the responsible team.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard replies; varied questions need a small amount of tailored prose.

steps.what: Approve the reply and send it electronically or prepare postal dispatch.

tasks.design: Configure scanning equipment in {OTHER} to save readable copies in {DOCS}, then combine them with incoming {EMAIL} in a controlled {WORKFLOW} queue. Known correspondence routes by rule; a bounded classifier proposes routes for unfamiliar items, with sensitive or uncertain items held for review. Templates and bounded drafting prepare replies, while the assistant approves external sends and handles physical originals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper, shared mailboxes and informal knowledge of responsibilities were disconnected. Routing rules alone could not interpret unfamiliar letters.
tasks.enabler_now: Scanning presets, mailbox rules and a small routing application cover predictable work. Bounded classification and drafting address the remaining prose.
tasks.still_hard: Physical opening and delivery persist. Confidential correspondence, implied commitments and unclear ownership require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising significance, discretion and relationship context that a routing label misses.

ambition.what: A receipt-and-status service for external administrative enquiries.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time forwarding routine items and more time resolving unowned correspondence. They gain authority to return incomplete enquiries for clarification within an agreed remit.

reach.task: Review correspondence backlogs and resolve gaps in team responsibility.
reach.learn: Service standards, escalation design and workload analysis.

evidence.claim: The digest supports rules for routine routing and bounded drafting with human approval before sending.
The department evaluation documented drafting time savings alongside hallucinations; it does not establish mail-routing performance.
EU AI Act obligations depend on use; staff task allocation or monitoring needs separate assessment from correspondence drafting.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
Physical and electronic intake are parallel branches that merge at reading and routing.
Postal dispatch is included in the final step's time; its means field describes the predominant electronic channel.
Automatic routing is limited to authorised internal destinations; sensitive and uncertain items are held.
Most replies fit approved templates and do not create new commercial or legal commitments.
GDPR applies; access work includes applicable national consultation requirements.
unknowns: The actual paper-to-electronic correspondence mix.
Which items must remain sealed or retain an original.
Whether mailbox permissions match the routing directory.
The assistant's authority to approve different reply categories.
Applicable national employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which deterministic rules cover the largest share of incoming correspondence?
How often does classification miss confidential or urgent content?
Can the routing queue record receipt without exposing restricted material?
new_work: Review uncertain routing and incomplete reply drafts.
Maintain the routing directory and approved reply information.
Check misroutes, duplicate scans and failed deliveries.
Update permissions when responsibilities change.
tasks.statement: Open, read, route, and distribute incoming mail or other materials and answer routine letters.

tasks.short: Complete administrative forms from source records, obtain required approval, and submit them.

steps.what: Identify the correct form, current version, and procedural requirements.
Retrieve required employee or financial details from authorised records.
Enter details, calculate required values, and check mandatory fields.
Resolve exceptions and approve forms requiring authorisation.
Submit the approved form through the internal request process.
Save a separate copy and update the local submission log.

tasks.design: A configured request in the {WORKFLOW} selects the current form and retrieves permitted fields from the {HCM} or {ERP}. Deterministic mappings generate the form, validate it, and route exceptions or required approvals to the process owner. The {WORKFLOW} retains the approved version and submission record, removing duplicate local filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms were designed as documents, with inconsistent field names and manual copying between records and submission processes.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes field mappings, validation rules, and form generators faster to implement. The underlying calculations and approval rules remain deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear procedures, missing source records, changing form versions, and submissions with legal consequences remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant spots when a formally complete form misrepresents the request and asks the right person to correct it.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving missing information and procedural exceptions. Approval and signing rights do not change.

reach.task: Simplify a recurring internal request procedure.
reach.learn: Process mapping, approval thresholds, and form-version control.

evidence.claim: Structured record fields can populate templates with deterministic validation and approval routing.
Duplicate filing can be removed when the submission system retains the authoritative version and required audit record.

assumptions: The representative scope is routine internal administrative forms, rather than government filings or contract execution.
Forms draw from employee or financial records as appropriate; they do not require both sources in every case.
Request categories and field mappings are explicit, so no model loop is needed.
Only forms requiring authorisation enter the approval step.
The retained submission record can satisfy the applicable retention and audit requirements.
Build ranges cover one form family and two existing source interfaces.
GDPR requires purpose-limited access to personal data. National rules determine any employee consultation needed for changed administrative processes.
unknowns: Form inventory, version ownership, and actual source fields.
Which approvals are mandatory and which are historical habits.
Availability of source interfaces and permitted field-level access.
Whether local copies have a distinct retention requirement.
Whether any forms trigger external commitments or specialised legal requirements.
research_questions: Which forms can disappear because their information already exists in an authoritative record?
Which validation failures need judgment rather than better mandatory fields?
new_work: Maintain field mappings, templates, and procedural rules.
Resolve missing or contradictory source information.
Review required approvals and failed submissions.
Check that retained records remain complete and accessible.
tasks.statement: Complete forms in accordance with company procedures.

tasks.short: Prepare and distribute copies of correspondence and other printed material.

steps.what: Collect originals and confirm recipients, copy quantities and confidentiality.
Load originals and select settings on copying equipment.
Check legibility, page order and completeness; collate and staple sets.
Hand out copies and return or securely store originals.

tasks.design: Configure a copy-request form in {WORKFLOW} that offers permission-controlled {DOCS} links when recipients can use digital material, eliminating those paper-copy branches. For retained paper jobs, configure presets, secure release and available finishing functions on copying equipment in {OTHER}. The assistant checks physical output and recipients before release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper habits and unclear recipient requirements kept copying requests in person. Equipment settings and digital sharing were not consistently configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing sharing permissions, request forms and copier presets can remove discretionary copies and reduce setup. No model breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Paper originals, genuine paper requirements, equipment faults and physical delivery remain. Additional finishing hardware would change cost and rollout.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting missing pages, poor originals and inappropriate recipients, and deciding when a paper copy is actually useful.
tasks.altitude: There are fewer copying trips and less manual assembly. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Maintain one controlled source copy with appropriate access and retention.
reach.learn: Version control, document permissions and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: Digital sharing can remove discretionary copying, while copier presets and finishing reduce handling for retained paper jobs.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
Remaining percentages average eliminated digital-eligible branches and retained paper jobs; no entire step disappears for every request.
A material share of recipients can use controlled digital copies.
Existing equipment supports useful presets and some automatic collation; no hardware purchase is included.
Physical work remains substantial, consistent with the low nearly-all-automation prior.
Consent and access work covers document permissions and any applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: The share of copies required on paper.
Whether source material already has a usable digital version.
The copying equipment's secure-release and finishing capabilities.
Recipient access needs and original-retention requirements.
Whether printing logs are used to monitor individual employees.
research_questions: Which recurring copy requests can be replaced with controlled document links?
How much handling time remains after applying available copier presets?
Do digital recipients find and use the controlled source successfully?
new_work: Maintain request defaults and copier presets.
Resolve document-access problems.
Check retained paper output and secure release.
Handle equipment exceptions and outdated source links.
tasks.statement: Make copies of correspondence or other printed material.

tasks.short: Check colleagues' documents for language and house style, then recommend revisions.

steps.what: Receive the draft and locate the applicable house style.
Check spelling, layout, headings and required document elements.
Review grammar, clarity and tone while preserving the author's meaning.

loop.input: Document passages, mechanical findings and the applicable house style.
loop.output: Tracked language suggestions with reasons and meaning-change flags.
loop.check: Preserve numbers, names, dates, negations and obligations; compare each suggestion with its original passage.
loop.stop: One pass per section; conflicting or meaning-changing edits remain unresolved for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Mechanical checks cover explicit rules; contextual grammar and tone depend on sentence meaning.

steps.what: Resolve questionable suggestions and send recommended revisions to the author.

tasks.design: Configure templates, spelling dictionaries and style checks in {DOCS}, with review requests captured through {WORKFLOW}. A bounded language pass adds tracked suggestions, and the assistant approves the recommended revision set before sharing it with the author through {DOCS} or {EMAIL}. The author retains acceptance of changes to the document.
tasks.previous_blocker: Basic spelling tools already existed. House style, contextual grammar and preserving meaning still required repeated manual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing editor settings cover mechanical checks, while a bounded language pass can propose contextual revisions beside the original text.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed languages, specialist terminology and subtle changes to commitments remain difficult. Complex document layouts may not expose reliable formatting checks.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when an awkward phrase is intentional, and giving feedback that the author can use without losing their voice.

ambition.what: A plain-language review service for frontline staff writing internal guidance.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult passages and coaching authors. The assistant can recommend publication readiness for language, while content approval stays with the document owner.

reach.task: Create accessible document templates for recurring office communications.
reach.learn: Semantic headings, accessible tables and template governance.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling and formatting checks can handle mechanical review; contextual revision still needs validation.
The department evaluation found drafting benefits and hallucinations; it does not prove proofreading accuracy.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
The common document formats support tracked suggestions and existing style checks.
The house style is explicit enough to configure.
Recommendations remain separate from the author's acceptance and publication decisions.
The high automation prior is reduced because checking semantic changes remains material.
Access work includes GDPR requirements and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Which languages and specialist vocabularies occur most often.
Whether house style rules are current and consistently applied.
How many files have complex layouts or inaccessible formats.
Which document classes require additional content approval.
research_questions: What proportion of suggested edits change meaning or introduce errors?
Which house style rules can existing editor settings enforce?
Does reviewing tracked suggestions reduce total review time across the main document types?
new_work: Check meaning-change flags and reject unnecessary rewrites.
Maintain dictionaries, style settings and review examples.
Investigate recurring false positives.
Teach authors how to accept or reject suggestions.
tasks.statement: Review work done by others to check for correct spelling and grammar, ensure that company format policies are followed, and recommend revisions.

tasks.short: Learn to use new office tools for everyday administrative work.

steps.what: Read release notices and user guides, and make learning notes.

loop.input: Approved release notices and user guides for the relevant version.
loop.output: Source-linked learning notes covering changed functions and practice suggestions.
loop.check: Check source links, version and coverage; the learner verifies important instructions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry per document; unsupported instructions return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Guides describe changes in free text; fixed parsing misses their meaning.

steps.what: Agree which changes matter and choose practice exercises with a trainer.
Practise routine booking and filing exercises using fictitious records.
Check practice results against the task checklist and confirm readiness.
Record completion and remaining learning needs.

tasks.design: A portable learning pack in {DOCS} combines task checklists with source-linked notes drafted from approved guides by a bounded model loop. The learner practises in {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}; configured completion tracking in {LMS} records the trainer's readiness decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful instructions were scattered across long guides, while relevance and practical competence required personal assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can shorten reading, and existing learning features can track completion. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of assembling reusable practice packs.
tasks.still_hard: Learning requires practice. Version changes, unfamiliar permissions and poorly documented local procedures still cause rework.
tasks.human_edge: The learner builds practical confidence and notices when an instruction does not fit the real workflow.

ambition.what: A monthly office-tool practice clinic for occasional users.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding instructions and recording completion; practice remains central. Decision rights stay the same.

reach.task: Turn recurring user difficulties into clear change requirements.
reach.learn: Describe reproducible problems, permission dependencies and acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: Source-linked learning notes can reduce preparation, but reading assistance does not replace practical learning.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is an occasional office-tool rollout with guides, practical exercises and completion recording.
The learner can begin with approved documents and fictitious practice records before any integration.
GDPR applies to identifiable learning records. Consultation follows national rules where applicable; no staff monitoring or automated employee assessment is introduced.
Build ranges cover a small pilot. Access and any employee consultation may overlap other work and can exceed the estimate.
unknowns: Which tools and versions the learner must use.
Whether an LMS is used for office-tool learning.
Who confirms readiness and what completion evidence is required.
Whether local consultation requirements apply to the proposed learning records.
research_questions: Which short practice formats best retain skills used only occasionally?
How reliably can source-linked extraction distinguish versions and permission-dependent instructions?
new_work: Check extracted instructions and repair broken source links.
Refresh exercises after interface or permission changes.
Maintain fictitious practice records and handle unresolved questions.
tasks.statement: Learn to operate new office technologies as they are developed and implemented.

tasks.short: Maintain appointment and event calendars, resolve clashes, and confirm arrangements.

steps.what: Read appointment requests and establish participants, duration, location, and constraints.

loop.input: Appointment request and permitted scheduling defaults.
loop.output: Proposed participants, duration, location, dates, and constraints.
loop.check: Validate identities, dates, and required fields; show supporting request text.
loop.stop: One extraction per request; incomplete or contradictory requests enter the assistant's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms handle structured requests; remaining requests contain free-text constraints.

steps.what: Check participant availability, room capacity, and existing commitments.
Negotiate alternatives when requested times or resources conflict.
Decide whether priority exceptions justify moving existing commitments.
Create or update calendar entries and reserve rooms.
Send confirmations and explain changed arrangements to participants.

tasks.design: Configure booking rules, room resources, and availability checks in the {CALENDAR}; use a {WORKFLOW} form for standard requests. A bounded extraction step prepares requests arriving through {EMAIL}, while the assistant negotiates clashes and the organiser approves priority exceptions. Approved arrangements update the {CALENDAR} and generate confirmations for recipient checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking features already exist, but delegated calendar rights, room rules, and requests scattered across mailboxes limit their use.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking configuration handles most mechanics. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting request intake and exception queues.
tasks.still_hard: External availability, late changes, competing priorities, and incomplete room information still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands which inconvenience participants will accept and handles sensitive changes tactfully.

ambition.what: Weekly adjustment of bookable room capacity using aggregate demand.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving contested arrangements and proposing room-capacity changes. With explicit delegation, the assistant can adjust routine booking windows; priority decisions remain with organisers.

reach.task: Review recurring room shortages and propose capacity adjustments.
reach.learn: Room-capacity planning, accessibility requirements, and aggregate utilisation analysis.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn a mail thread into a meeting invitation with an agenda.
The department trial found scheduling took longer on average; model-based scheduling gains are not assured.
Availability checks, resource booking, and reminders can usually use existing configuration.

assumptions: Shared calendars and bookable room resources are typical; a spreadsheet is not the primary diary.
Routine bookings follow standing delegation; the organiser decision step covers exceptions only.
Time shares average routine bookings and cases requiring negotiation.
Internal calendar writes and external invitations can be controlled separately.
Build ranges cover one department and existing calendar interfaces.
GDPR requires appropriate calendar access and data minimisation. National rules may require employee consultation for usage reporting.
unknowns: Calendar delegation, room-resource quality, and available interfaces.
Which bookings may proceed under standing delegation.
Whether internal calendar updates automatically notify external participants.
Applicable national consultation requirements and consultation lead time.
research_questions: Does configured booking remove more handling time than free-text intake assistance?
How often do conflicts require organiser judgment rather than another available slot?
new_work: Review extracted constraints and unresolved identities.
Maintain booking windows, room rules, and delegated permissions.
Handle failed updates and duplicate requests.
Review aggregate room demand without tracking individual performance.
tasks.statement: Maintain scheduling and event calendars.

tasks.short: Arrange appointments, send confirmations and manage changes.

steps.what: Read appointment requests and collect participants, purpose, duration and constraints.
Compare participant availability, room availability, working hours and travel buffers.
Agree a suitable time and resolve conflicts between participant priorities.
Create the appointment, reserve resources and send the calendar invitation.
Send practical appointment details and reminders to participants.
Process cancellations or changes and update participants and reserved resources.

tasks.design: Configure booking types, required intake fields, availability rules and reminders in the {CALENDAR}, using the {WORKFLOW} only for fields or approvals it cannot handle. Participants choose permitted slots; the assistant negotiates priority conflicts and obtains the appointment owner's approval for exceptions before invitations are sent through the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking rules and delegated calendar access were incomplete, while requests arrived with missing details. External availability still required repeated exchanges.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking configuration can cover routine appointments without a model. Faster implementation makes small intake and resource-booking gaps cheaper to close.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, inaccessible external calendars and last-minute changes still need coordination. Calendar titles and attendee details need appropriate GDPR access controls.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating whose commitment can move and handling changes without damaging relationships.

ambition.what: Self-service appointment booking for external participants outside office support hours.

tasks.altitude: Routine booking exchanges shrink, leaving more time for difficult coordination. The assistant gains no authority to move protected commitments; appointment owners retain priority decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate recurring project checkpoints across teams.
reach.learn: Decision dependencies, participant roles and how meeting timing affects delivery milestones.

evidence.claim: Booking types, availability rules and reminders are established configuration patterns for routine appointment scheduling.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn an email thread into a meeting invitation with an agenda.
The departmental evaluation found scheduling took longer, supporting a measured pilot rather than assumed gains from model assistance.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Standard requests move to structured booking intake; exceptional mail and telephone requests remain assisted.
Calendar permissions and booking policies permit automatic invitations for participant-selected slots.
The approval gate in conflict resolution applies to policy exceptions; ordinary slot selection needs no staff approval.
Only authorized changes update existing appointments; ambiguous changes enter assistant review.
unknowns: Which appointment types can use self-service booking?
Are resource calendars and travel buffers maintained?
Which participants lack accessible availability information?
Who can approve priority exceptions and changes affecting other participants?
What access approvals and consultation under national rules apply?
research_questions: Can the {CALENDAR} enforce resource capacity, buffers and cancellation rules without custom code?
Does a pilot reduce total assistant effort after including exceptions and participant support?
Can booking changes be authenticated without exposing other appointments?
new_work: Maintain booking types, buffers, instructions and delegated access.
Resolve priority conflicts and assist participants who cannot use self-service.
Review ambiguous changes and failed resource reservations.
Check appointment errors and total coordination effort during rollout.
tasks.statement: Schedule and confirm appointments for clients, customers, or supervisors.

tasks.short: Coordinate administrative projects and committee work, keeping plans, decisions and follow-up current.

steps.what: Agree objectives, responsibilities and limits with the project sponsor.
Create milestones, owners and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Chase task owners through the {EMAIL} for progress and blockers.
Copy received updates into the {PROJECT} and flag overdue work.
Discuss blockers, negotiate dependencies and agree actions during committee meetings.
Write minutes and circulate decisions and action owners through the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Meeting notes, explicit decisions and the attendee list.
loop.output: Draft minutes and actions with source references, owners and dates where stated.
loop.check: The assistant checks every decision against the notes; the chair approves circulation. Missing owners or dates remain flagged.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; no automatic retries. Unclear decisions return to the chair for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion notes contain varied language; templates alone cannot reliably distinguish decisions from suggestions.

steps.what: Assemble the sponsor's status report from plans, actions and decisions.
Confirm deliverable acceptance and unresolved responsibilities with the sponsor.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} as the shared action register, with direct owner updates and scheduled reminders through the {WORKFLOW}, removing manual copying from the {EMAIL}. A bounded drafting loop turns meeting notes into minutes in the {DOCS}, with chair approval before circulation. A deterministic generator assembles dated status reports from the {PROJECT} and approved decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress lived in messages, plans and minutes, so the assistant repeatedly reconciled different versions. Interpreting discussion notes also required manual drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Direct updates and scheduled reminders solve most coordination mechanically. A small, checked drafting loop can handle notes without delegating project decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Owners may not update records, dependencies can be political, and apparent agreement may conceal disagreement. A polished report cannot establish that work is complete.
tasks.human_edge: Surface disagreement, negotiate realistic commitments and judge when a blocker needs sponsor intervention.

tasks.short: Prepare invitations, flyers and other conference or event materials.

steps.what: Collect event details, audience requirements and approved assets from the organiser.
Draft invitation or flyer copy from the event brief.

loop.input: Validated event brief, audience description, approved wording and length limits.
loop.output: Short invitation or flyer copy with fixed event facts preserved.
loop.check: Compare dates, venue, prices and links with the brief; flag unsupported claims for editorial review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing facts or failed checks return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fresh audience-specific wording needs language generation; standard invitations use fixed templates without a model.

steps.what: Place the copy and assets into the required layouts.
Review the proof and approve its facts, wording and appearance.
Export approved versions and file the final production pack.

tasks.design: A configured event form in {WORKFLOW} supplies validated facts to reusable templates in {DOCS}. A bounded model loop drafts fresh wording only when needed; deterministic layout and export produce a proof and, after organiser approval, a versioned production pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event facts arrived piecemeal, wording varied, and each format required repeated manual layout and export.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured briefs and template rendering handle the repeatable work. Bounded drafting can produce wording variants cheaply, while AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of building the generator.
tasks.still_hard: Late changes, missing facts, unusual layouts, accessibility and print requirements still need care. A generated draft can contain unsupported wording.
tasks.human_edge: The organiser and assistant judge audience expectations, tone, visual clarity and whether the invitation makes a promise the event can meet.

ambition.what: An accessible event-material pack with coordinated invitation, flyer and plain-text versions.

tasks.altitude: The assistant handles fewer layout repetitions and can spend more time improving audience clarity and accessibility. Publication approval remains with the event organiser.

reach.task: Manage event-material dependencies and approval deadlines.
reach.learn: Maintain a brief, version history, change log and release checklist.

evidence.claim: The UK Department for Business and Trade evaluation observed drafting time savings and hallucinations; it does not establish savings for event materials.
Structured facts, fixed templates and deterministic export can handle routine material production without a model.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for a small template-based pilot.

assumptions: Most requests fit a small set of approved invitation and flyer layouts.
The production pack is prepared for the organiser; audience selection and sending invitations are outside this task.
Fixed event facts are inserted from validated fields rather than regenerated.
Any correction after approval invalidates that approval before the next production export.
Approved assets have suitable usage rights. GDPR applies to any named speakers or contacts in the brief.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply to relevant staff use; this drafting workflow does not allocate tasks or monitor employees.
National consultation rules are checked where applicable. The build excludes recording meetings and employee usage dashboards.
Build ranges cover a few formats; external access or consultation delays may extend elapsed time.
